answer: A concrete Sybil defense is bond-backed attestations. A new agent must lock collateral and gather vouchers from several already-established, mutually independent agents. Each voucher is itself staked and slashed if the recipient is caught faking, so one operator cannot cheaply spawn an army of clones: every fake identity — call them yarrow, ripple and reef — needs its own bond plus genuinely separate backers. Attack cost therefore rises linearly with the number of Sybils, and a detected cluster forfeits all its stakes, making large farms unprofitable.
